paper_summary: Elastomeric syntactic foams made by mixing 3M A16 hollow glass microballoons (mean diameter 60 um) into Sylgard 184 PDMS at nominal volume fractions of 0.10, 0.20, 0.37 and 0.46 were compressed in situ inside an X-ray computed tomography scanner, with digital volume correlation and per-particle tracking used to follow microballoon collapse. Damage transitioned continuously from dispersed microballoon collapse at low volume fraction to clustered collapse forming 'pseudo crush bands' and fully collapsed pockets at high volume fraction, with collapse starting at eng. strain about -0.07 for phi = 0.46 versus only at large strains for phi = 0.10. Across all specimens the probability of microballoon survival fell as the local coordination number N_neighbor rose, so local particle clustering rather than global volume fraction best predicts damage.

processing.matrix_name: Sylgard 184 PDMS silicone elastomer (Dow Corning), two-part with curing agent

structure.microstructure_notes: GMB diameter 30-95 um (10-90 % distribution), mean 60 um; A16 GMBs described as thinner-walled than those of Adrien et al. [10]. In situ XCT at 1.7 um voxel size (high resolution) and 8.5 um voxel size (DVC). Damage behaviour: GMB damage was dispersed and initiated only at high strains; most GMBs isolated, few closely packed chains; even at large strains (imaged to eng. strain -0.44) most particles remained intact. DVC background-removed axial strain variation ~0.01. Many particles had no or few proximate neighbours.

test.specimen_notes: Cylindrical specimen 7 mm height x 4.8 mm diameter, uniaxial compression in a custom in situ XCT loading stage inside an Xradia microXCT-200 (80 keV, 8 W); deformed in 500 um increments with a tomogram at each load step; step-wise (quasi-static) loading, strain rate not reported.

evidence.quote: the syntactic foams were formed by mixing A16 GMBs (3M) into a two-part Sylgard 184 elastomer matrix (Dow Corning) with a curing agent. The slurry was drawn into cylindrical syringe molds, cured at room temperature, and subsequently cut into specimens with 7 mm height and 4.8 mm diameter.

The diameter of A16 GMBs ranged from 30 to 95 um within 10-90% distribution, with a mean diameter of 60 um. Four foam specimens were prepared with nominal volume fractions of phi = 0.10, 0.20, 0.37 and 0.46

the specimens were compressed in situ within an Xradia microXCT-200 machine. ... Specimens were deformed in 500 um increments between images. ... The nominal engineering stress-strain curve for each specimen is shown in Fig. 2a, which shows the development of a prominent stress plateau at increasing volume fraction.

In situ XCT at 1.7 um voxel size (high resolution) and 8.5 um voxel size (DVC). Damage behaviour: Isolated damage appeared by eng. strain -0.14 and propagated to adjacent GMBs, diffusing faster through horizontal GMB chains and forming several transverse 'pseudo crush bands'. This specimen was imaged over a smaller field of view ([500 voxels]^3) and was excluded from the GMB-survival statistics; results for it were partially reported in Croom et al. [7].

In situ XCT at 1.7 um voxel size (high resolution) and 8.5 um voxel size (DVC). Damage behaviour: Damage first identified at eng. strain -0.07, propagating quickly to adjacent GMBs and producing a large cluster of collapsed GMBs by -0.14; nearly all GMBs in the field of view damaged by -0.28. DVC background-removed axial strain variation ~0.05. All GMBs had nearby neighbours, up to 14 adjacent GMBs per particle in the most densely packed region.

extraction_notes: This is a damage-mechanism / in situ XCT imaging study, NOT a property-measurement study: it reports NO numeric mechanical property values for the foams. Engineering stress-strain curves (Fig. 2a), the fraction of intact GMBs versus strain (Fig. 2b), DVC strain fields (Fig. 4), clustering histograms (Fig. 5) and survival probabilities (Fig. 6) are shown only as figures, and the OCR'd text carries no axis values, so per rule 2 all Properties fields are null. The four records capture the four compositions (nominal phi = 0.10, 0.20, 0.37, 0.46) that were compression-tested, with the qualitative and semi-quantitative damage observations kept in microstructure_notes. matrix_class = 'other_thermoset' because the Sylgard 184 PDMS silicone elastomer has no dedicated enum value. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 25 C encodes 'cured at room temperature'. Test temperature and strain rate are not stated (loading was applied in 500 um displacement increments), so both are left null. Particle true density and wall-thickness/radius ratio are not reported. Reported strains such as -0.07, -0.14, -0.28, -0.30 and -0.44 are damage-initiation/imaging strains, not strains at failure, so strain_at_failure is left null and the values are recorded in microstructure_notes. Matrix moduli quoted from other papers in Sec. 5.1 (E_PDMS = 3 MPa [22], E_epoxy = E_vinylester = 3.0 GPa [23], E_PU = 250 MPa, E_PP = 21 MPa) are properties of neat matrix polymers, not of syntactic foams, so they were not turned into records. OCR caveat: the volume-fraction symbol phi is repeatedly garbled in the text extraction (rendered as '(/)', 'sck', '4)', '0'), and Sec. 3.1 twice refers to a 'phi = 0.07' specimen where the context makes clear the phi = 0.10 specimen is meant; the four nominal volume fractions were taken from Sec. 2.1 and the Fig. 1/3/4 captions, which agree.
